Definition: from G2957; i.e. Cyrenæan, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene:--of Cyrene, Cyrenian.
BiblicalUsage: Men of Cyrene are the believers from North Africa, and the most famous of them carried the cross. In Matthew 27:32, Mark 15:21, and Luke 23:26 Simon a Cyrenian is compelled to bear Jesus' cross, in Acts 6:9 Cyrenians dispute with Stephen, and in Acts 11:20 men of Cyprus and Cyrene preach the Lord Jesus at Antioch.
TheologicalSignificance: For me, Simon of Cyrene is the picture of the disciple: a man pulled from the crowd and made to carry the cross after Jesus, and his sons Alexander and Rufus are named because the church knew them. A man pulled from the crowd became the picture of the disciple.
